events.summary: A fire broke out around 04:00 on 18 June 2022 at the chemicals division; one person died and one was lightly injured. The company then shut its crude refining and ethylene units.
events.effect: Company spokesperson (via Reuters/Arab News): it 'has shut its crude oil refining and ethylene units to evaluate safety risks', duration unspecified. Company notice (NBD, 19 June): main production units were shut down in an orderly way and it was preparing them for restart.
events.threshold_basis: Refinery crude units shut after a fire, as the operator reported.

recovery.evidence: Sinopec 'has partially restarted operations' at the 320,000-bpd Shanghai refinery (QCintel headline and lead). Full restart date not found.

events.summary: During a prolonged heatwave and drought that cut hydropower output, Sichuan's industry department and State Grid Sichuan jointly issued an emergency notice on 14 Aug 2022 ordering all industrial power users on the orderly-power-use list in 19 of the province's 21 prefecture-level units to halt production from 15 to 20 Aug, safety loads excepted.
events.effect: Order text (The Paper, Jiemian): full production halt for all listed industrial users, including white-listed priority firms, 00:00 15 Aug to 24:00 20 Aug. AP (17 Aug): factories shut or cut output; timed power cuts of 2.5 to 3 hours were reported in one city. CGTN (18 Aug) described a provincial notice to some high-capacity enterprises, with a production halt from 14 to 20 Aug and about 7 million kW released for residential use. Jiemian: one listed chemicals firm expected about 35,000 t less urea. Al Jazeera (22 Aug): power rationing in southwestern China to continue until at least 25 Aug, according to local media and factories.
events.threshold_basis: Clause 5: grid-operator emergency notice (State Grid Sichuan, jointly with the provincial department) ordering an industrial load shed in 19 of the province's 21 prefecture-level units; also clause 4, a generation shortfall with timed cuts reported in one city.

capacity_affected.unit: prefecture-level units under an ordered full industrial production halt
capacity_affected.source_says: 实施生产全停（保安负荷除外）

events.facility_name_local: 内蒙古阿拉善新井煤业有限公司露天煤矿
events.operator: Inner Mongolia Alxa Xinjing Coal Industry Co Ltd
events.summary: A catastrophic slope collapse at an open-pit coal mine in Inner Mongolia killed 53 and injured 6. The State Council-approved investigation classed it as a particularly serious production-safety liability accident and recommended a special nationwide campaign to find and fix major mine-safety hazards.
events.effect: Cailian Press (23 Feb): all local coal mines halted production for hazard checks. Reuters via Kitco (9 May, citing a 24 Apr document it could not independently verify, and Mysteel): 32 open-pit mines in Inner Mongolia with 26.55 Mt of capacity halted, and 23.55 Mt of planned expansions paused.
events.threshold_basis: Coal-mine disaster followed by reported mine halts with stated capacity. No output reduction was reported; the capacity figure rests on a document Reuters could not verify.

capacity_affected.unit: million tonnes/year coal production capacity halted (32 open-pit mines)
capacity_affected.source_says: the mines have 26.55 million tonnes of production capacity; document dated April 24 could not be independently verified by Reuters

events.operator: Shanxi Tongzhou Coal & Coke Group (山西通洲集团)
events.summary: A gas explosion at 19:29 on 22 May 2026 at the Liushenyu coal mine in Shanxi killed 82 and left 2 missing. The operator's four mines were ordered to halt, and widespread safety inspections across Shanxi suspended mining capacity.
events.effect: Xinhua: 责令山西通洲集团下属四座煤矿全部停产整顿 (all four of the group's mines ordered to halt for rectification). Sxcoal citing NBS: Shanxi raw coal output in June 2026 was 78.01 Mt, down 31.5% y/y, attributed to the explosion and the resulting suspensions. Reuters: national June output fell 9.7% y/y, the steepest drop since 2016. Xinhua (Oct 2026): Shanxi output fell more than 30% y/y in each month from June to August.
events.threshold_basis: Coal-mine disaster followed by a reported, quantified provincial supply cut (clause 7 also met).

capacity_affected.unit: percent y/y fall in Shanxi raw coal output, June 2026
capacity_affected.source_says: 78.01 million tonnes, down 31.5% year on year (Sxcoal, NBS data)

recovery.evidence: A province-wide report of mines resuming after rectification was read; it does not mention the accident mine or its operator. No restart report for this mine was found.
